races.paceDynamic: Independent Jimmy will control this race from the front with no other natural pace-setters to challenge him early. The McCain runner can dictate a comfortable tempo through the early stages before quickening approaching the business end. With most of the field holding up, including Universal Secret, King Of The Story, and Jiair Madrik, the pace will be modest early but accelerate sharply from three out. This shape strongly favours prominent runners and those with tactical pace who can position closer to Independent Jimmy, as the hold-up brigade will face a wall of horses when the sprint develops.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Independent Jimmy gets an uncontested lead and dictates fractions
scenarios.body: Jimmy can string out the field turning for home while Universal Secret and King Of The Story get first run on the leaders. The hold-up horses get caught behind the pace injection and struggle to make ground in time.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow early and the field bunches approaching two out
scenarios.body: Universal Secret's proven finishing kick from the back becomes decisive as King Of The Story also benefits from the condensed finish. The front runner gets swamped by superior class.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Drama
scenarios.trigger: If Independent Jimmy compounds or makes jumping errors under pressure
scenarios.body: Quickasican and King Of Cong can capitalise from their prominent positions as the race falls apart. The hold-up horses still get hampered by the carnage ahead.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Package
scenarios.trigger: If the headgear changes work dramatically for the outsiders
scenarios.body: Ironica De Thaix finds her jumping or Sawpit Samantha benefits from the pace setup despite poor recent form. An unlikely but possible outcome given the competitive handicap nature.

watchPoints.text: Independent Jimmy's jumping after 169-day layoff could determine if he maintains his crucial early advantage
Universal Secret needs the pace to develop properly from his hold-up style or he'll have too much to do
Quickasican was pulled up just 14 days ago and trainer Bedi is 0/9 in last 14 days
Ironica De Thaix has been pulled up three consecutive times and cheekpieces failed to help last time
King Of The Story's jumping quality will be crucial from his hold-up position in a competitive field

races.paceDynamic: Final Surprise will take up a clear lead with Solo Eclipse, Double Tiger, Beau Quali, and The Hostage all wanting prominent positions early, creating traffic congestion. The genuine pace from Final Surprise should ensure a true gallop throughout, but the bunching of four prominent runners behind him will create tactical problems approaching the business end. The sustained pace will stretch out the field, with the hold-up horses getting a genuine pace to aim at. This race shape strongly favours the hold-up merchants who can avoid the early traffic and benefit from the strong gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Brigade Thrives
scenarios.trigger: If Final Surprise maintains honest pace and prominent quartet get in each other's way
scenarios.body: The genuine gallop will suit closers who can navigate around the early scrimmaging, with stamina coming to the fore over this extended trip. Manalishi and Chicker are ideally positioned to strike late having avoided the congestion.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Prevails Early
scenarios.trigger: If one of the quartet breaks clear from the pack approaching two out
scenarios.body: Solo Eclipse or Double Tiger could capitalize on their forward positions if they jump fluently and avoid the worst of the traffic. The winner would need to resist the late challenge from hold-up horses who get a clear run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Final Surprise Stays Strong
scenarios.trigger: If the pace-setter maintains his rhythm and the penalty proves manageable
scenarios.body: His recent course win gives Final Surprise the confidence to resist all-comers, particularly if the prominent group neutralize each other. The 7lb penalty becomes irrelevant if he can dictate terms from the front throughout.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers or interference causes major disruption at a crucial flight
scenarios.body: The race becomes a lottery with positioning at obstacles paramount rather than pure ability. Any horse getting a clear passage benefits while class horses get hampered by the mayhem.

watchPoints.text: Final Surprise could get loose on the lead if the prominent quartet get too focused on each other early
Traffic problems likely approaching third last hurdle where Uttoxeter track starts to turn for home
Manalishi and Chicker both need clean jumps throughout to maximize their hold-up advantage
Beau Quali's recent yard switch could yield immediate improvement given his proven ability
Solo Eclipse returning from lengthy break under inexperienced jockey creates potential for errors

races.paceDynamic: Barry Fife will take this small field along at a steady gallop over this extended trip, with Crack Ops, Country Mouse and the other prominent runners content to track closely behind. The lack of confirmed front-runners beyond Barry Fife means no genuine pace pressure until the business end, creating a rhythm that builds gradually through the race. Only Galway Reel represents hold-up tactics, but Sean Bowen will need to position him carefully in such a small field. This tactical setup strongly favours prominent racers who can sit handy and have something left for the finish, rather than pure speed horses or those needing a strong gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If Barry Fife sets reasonable fractions without being pressured early
scenarios.body: The race becomes a tactical affair where horses tracking in second and third get first run on the leader turning for home. Crack Ops and Country Mouse are perfectly positioned to exploit this, having the class and recent form to capitalize.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sustainable Pace Suits
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely steady and nobody commits too early
scenarios.body: The lack of pace pressure allows Barry Fife to dictate throughout and kick clear when it matters, while Galway Reel gets the perfect setup for his hold-up style. Both benefit from the tactical nature but different running styles prosper.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Class Rises To Top
scenarios.trigger: If the small field splits the difference tactically with moderate early pace
scenarios.body: The race becomes about pure ability rather than tactics, suiting the highest-rated performers who can quicken when required. Crack Ops has shown the best recent hurdles form while Galway Reel brings chase experience back to the smaller obstacles.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Long Absence Backfires
scenarios.trigger: If either Galway Reel or Dexperado shows ring-rustiness from extended layoffs
scenarios.body: Their fitness concerns become evident in the final furlong, allowing the more race-fit prominent runners to come through strongly. The regularly campaigned horses take advantage of their sharper condition in a tactical finish.

watchPoints.text: Galway Reel could be positioned too far back by Sean Bowen in this small field, making his hold-up style ineffective
Barry Fife's jumping needs monitoring as any mistakes will disrupt his front-running tactics and hand initiative to trackers
Crack Ops showed jumping errors last time at Bangor, any repeat issues will cost him dearly in a tactical finish
The pace early will determine everything - if Barry Fife goes too slow it hands the advantage to Galway Reel
Market support for either Dexperado or Pepite De Saphir would suggest their lengthy absences aren't concerns to connections

races.paceDynamic: Skyjack Hijack will set the pace from the front with minimal pressure in this small field of hold-up horses. With only Geezer Rockstar likely to race prominently early, Skyjack Hijack can dictate a comfortable tempo through the first half of this 2m7½f test. The lack of pace pressure means the leaders can conserve energy for a sustained finish, while the six hold-up horses will need to rely on late kicks from potentially compromised positions. This race shape strongly favors front-runners and prominent racers who can avoid traffic problems and capitalize on the soft early pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Skyjack Hijack Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Skyjack Hijack maintains his jumping rhythm and isn't pressured for pace
scenarios.body: The 8yo can use his class from his 2024 winning streak to control the race from pillar to post, while the hold-up brigade struggle to make up ground on the leaders who've had an easy time of it. His 441-day absence is a concern but the tactical advantage is enormous.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely slow and bunches the field for a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows patient riders like Sean Bowen and Gavin Sheehan to time their challenges perfectly, with Secret Trix and Super Survivor using their class to sweep past tiring leaders. The good ground suits these staying types who can quicken late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Minella Rescue Repeats
scenarios.trigger: If Minella Rescue's course form and tactical speed proves decisive in the straight
scenarios.body: The 2025 course winner can use James Davies' tactical nous to position perfectly and strike at the optimum moment, benefiting from both the race shape and proven course ability. His 35-day break should have him spot-on for this exact test.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Skyjack Hijack's lengthy absence tells and he fades dramatically from the front
scenarios.body: The leader's capitulation creates a messy finish where any horse with a clear run can capitalize, potentially allowing an outsider like Wa Wa or Kayf Dancer to sneak through. Positioning becomes crucial as the field concertinas in the final furlong.

watchPoints.text: Skyjack Hijack's jumping early - any mistakes will end his tactical advantage immediately
Secret Trix and Super Survivor's positioning turning in - both need clear runs from hold-up positions
Minella Rescue's early tracking position - James Davies must judge the pace perfectly to repeat last year's win
The pace through the first mile - if genuinely slow it will completely change the complexion of the finish
Geezer Rockstar's willingness to race prominently - could provide crucial early pace support for Skyjack Hijack

races.paceDynamic: Orderoftheday is the sole confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the flag in this small field. With no other natural pace angles, he'll get an uncontested lead and can bowl along at a sustainable rhythm that suits his style. The three hold-up horses (Queensbury Boy, Black Hawk Eagle, Stanners Glen) and prominent runner That's Nice will track behind, creating a bunched field turning for home. This setup clearly favours the front runner who can control the tempo without pressure, making life difficult for the closers who need a strong pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Orderoftheday gets an easy lead and maintains his jumping rhythm
scenarios.body: He can dictate ideal fractions and kick clear when the field comes to him turning in. The lack of pace pressure allows him to save energy for a decisive move when challenged.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Rally Catches Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too slow and Orderoftheday ties up in the final half-mile
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get the strong gallop they need when the tempo lifts approaching the last few fences. Queensbury Boy and Black Hawk Eagle can use their superior ratings.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If That's Nice can sit handy and benefit from her Nicky Henderson stable momentum
scenarios.body: She can travel sweetly in behind Orderoftheday and strike when he comes back to her. Her hurdles form suggests she has the class when things go right.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Jumping Errors Decide
scenarios.trigger: If the favourite or leader makes a crucial mistake at a key fence
scenarios.body: The race opens up for whichever horse is traveling best and jumping most fluently in behind. Stanners Glen's recent hurdles win suggests he's in form.

watchPoints.text: Orderoftheday's jumping under pressure - any significant mistake hands initiative to closers
Black Hawk Eagle's temperament after his fall last time, could be keen early and compromise his hold-up style
Queensbury Boy's breathing post-wind surgery, particularly in the final half-mile when race tempo lifts
That's Nice's fence technique in the back straight, she's made errors in recent chase starts
Stanners Glen's inexperience over fences when the pace quickens, jumping will determine his chance

races.name: Somersby Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Victoria Milano
runners_data.note: Front-runner with wind surgery behind her, 42 days off could have her fresh but needs to prove effectiveness after recent disappointments
runners_data.comment: Won two novices for Alistair Ralph in 2023-24; mainly disappointing since; bit to prove
runners_data.spotlight: Won two novice hurdles (2m3f/2m) for Alistair Ralph in 2023-24; rather disappointing since, including on her three starts for this yard after wind surgery last season (pulled up over fences last time); bit to prove.

runners_data.name: Nitty Gritty
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with visor back on after encouraging Kelso second, 10-day turnaround suggests confidence but needs pace to aim at
runners_data.comment: Ex-Irish; maiden hurdle winner; good second in Kelso h'cap last week; each-way chance
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-Irish maiden hurdle winner; best two runs for Mark Walford have been in 2m3f handicaps, including last week when second at Kelso (good; visor back on and retained); each-way chance.

runners_data.name: Kingdom Of Stars
runners_data.note: Prominent runner unexposed over hurdles, hood worn when best, 40-day break ideal for Kerry Lee charge
runners_data.comment: 2m AW Flat winner; unexposed as a hurdler, best form at 2m3f; 2m too short on h'cap debut
runners_data.spotlight: 2m AW Flat winner for Tom Ward; unexposed as a hurdler, best run when 13l third in a Hereford novice in March (2m3f, good; wore a hood); wasn't suited by the drop back to 2m when pulled up on handicap debut last time; cheekpieces now tried again (no improvement with them on the Flat).

runners_data.name: Good Boy Griff
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who ran career-best when second at Bangor, Sean Bowen booking significant for Gary Hanmer stable
runners_data.comment: Improved on handicap debut when a short-head second at Bangor latest; chance on that form
runners_data.spotlight: Showed improved form on his handicap debut when a short-head second to a previous winner at Bangor last time (2m3f, good);  chance on that run.

runners_data.name: Sumatran Tiger
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from 169-day break, previous Huntingdon second suggests ability but long absence concerning
runners_data.comment: Six Flat wins; 2nd in a mares' novice hurdle; only 9th on h'cap debut; back after wind op
runners_data.spotlight: Six-time Flat winner; second in a mares' novice hurdle at Huntingdon in November (2m3f, good) but well beaten on handicap debut at Doncaster last time (2m3f, good to soft); returns having had wind surgery, but with a bit to prove.

runners_data.name: Legendary Day
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose recent form disappointing, first-time tongue-tie might spark improvement for Barry Brennan
runners_data.comment: Chase/hurdle/Flat winner; chance on his best form, but below par on last two runs
runners_data.spotlight: Chase/hurdle winner who won on the AW at Lingfield in February 2025; hasn't been in top form on his last couple of runs over hurdles; on a fair mark now.

runners_data.name: Whenthemusicstops

runners_data.comment: Best run when fifth in a Perth maiden in October; can do better on h'cap debut; chance
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed; second in two maiden hurdles (beaten 43l last time) but best effort when fifth in a Perth maiden in October (2m4f, soft); improvement likely on handicap debut with a tongue-tie tried; chance.

runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making stable debut after 191 days off, fading finish pattern makes him vulnerable at this trip
runners_data.comment: Modest form over hurdles and a chase for Philip Kirby; improvement needed on stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Modest form over hurdles and in a chase for Philip Kirby; needs to take a big step forward on this stable debut.

runners_data.spotlight: Ex-Tom Lacey; well beaten in two handicaps for present yard following a long absence; needs to improve.

runners_data.spotlight: 0-11 over hurdles but ran a sound race last time on second run back from a break when clear second over 2m7f here; drops back in trip but a possible.

runners_data.spotlight: Won an Irish point in April 2025 (3m, good to yielding); three ordinary runs over 2m over hurdles; likely to improve markedly for step up in trip and cheekpieces on h'cap debut; a possible.

runners_data.spotlight: Poor form in three runs over hurdles, including when back after a wind op last time; blinkers tried on handicap debut; stiff task from 10lb out of the weights

races.paceDynamic: Victoria Milano will lead from flag to finish without pressure, being the only confirmed front-runner in this field. The prominent runners Kingdom Of Stars, Legendary Day, Whenthemusicstops and Fighting Falcon will track her in second gear, creating a modest gallop through the early stages. With so many hold-up horses including Nitty Gritty, Good Boy Griff, Sumatran Tiger and others relying on late kicks, the pace will be steady rather than searching. This sustainable tempo strongly favours the prominent runners who can position close enough to strike when Victoria Milano weakens, rather than the army of hold-up horses who will find insufficient pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Victoria Milano sets a steady tempo and the prominent horses track her comfortably
scenarios.body: Kingdom Of Stars and Whenthemusicstops can position perfectly to pounce when the leader tires in the straight. Their tactical advantage over the hold-up brigade becomes decisive in a steadily-run race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Lasts Home
scenarios.trigger: If Victoria Milano maintains her rhythm and the field fails to apply enough pressure
scenarios.body: Her uncontested lead becomes unassailable as the hold-up horses struggle to make up ground in the closing stages. The 42-day break could have her primed for a bold showing.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Surges
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is quicker than expected or Victoria Milano folds early
scenarios.body: Good Boy Griff or Nitty Gritty can produce their trademark late kicks to maximum effect. The faster tempo sets up perfectly for their closing styles to be most potent.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the race becomes a tactical crawl and the main fancies disappoint
scenarios.body: Saint Vic drops in trip but showed promise over longer last time, while Sumatran Tiger's class could tell. The steady pace allows an unfancied runner to sneak through.

watchPoints.text: Victoria Milano could get an uncontested lead and prove hard to peg back if her wind surgery has worked effectively
Good Boy Griff has Sean Bowen up and showed career-best form last time but needs sufficient pace to close into from his hold-up style
Kingdom Of Stars is unexposed in handicaps and could surprise if Kerry Lee has him ready after the 40-day break
Multiple horses carrying fading finish warnings including Earlofbrackenstown, Eskimo Sam, Fighting Falcon and Stay Hopeful make them risky propositions
Nitty Gritty has the visor back on after his Kelso second and the quick 10-day turnaround suggests Mark Walford confidence

races.name: Hobgoblin Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Spartan Times
runners_data.note: Only confirmed leader but proven at trip/track with 5lb claimer aboard, likely to get soft lead
runners_data.comment: Battled well to win big-field Uttoxeter handicap this month and is now 2-4 over hurdles
runners_data.spotlight: Fair Flat racer who battled well to win 16-runner handicap hurdle at Uttoxeter (2m, good) this month, after a break, and is now 2-4 in this sphere; 5lb claimer William Shanahan is enlisted today; high on the list.

runners_data.name: Castle Quarter
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 53-day break, won over C&D off this mark last May with headgear
runners_data.comment: AW Flat winner; 1-14 over hurdles, his win coming over C&D last May; not so good since
runners_data.spotlight: AW Flat winner; only win in 14 runs over hurdles was off this mark over C&D last May (good) when wearing a hood for the first time (as well as cheekpieces); hasn't done quite as well since, with today's combination of headgear the last twice.

runners_data.name: Zafaan
runners_data.note: Patient hold-up type returning from 180-day absence, consistent hurdler with strong C&D form
runners_data.comment: Dual Flat winner; placed in 5 of his 7 races over hurdles; interesting with Sean Bowen on
runners_data.spotlight: Dual Flat winner (1m/1m2f); placed in five of his seven races over hurdles, latest over C&D in October (good); ran with hood and cheekpieces that day but has neither this time; back after 180-day break; interesting with Sean Bowen booked.

runners_data.name: Roarin' Success
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with 3lb claimer, best hurdles effort was runner-up at Newcastle in novice company
runners_data.comment: Useful Flat handicapper; 2nd in Newcastle novice in January; non-runner at Aintree Friday
runners_data.spotlight: Useful Flat handicapper; best run over hurdles when runner-up in a novice at Newcastle in January; fair form on the Flat since following a wind op; non-runner 8.05 Aintree Friday.

runners_data.name: Collanisi
runners_data.note: Prominent type making handicap debut, limited hurdling form but interesting off low mark
runners_data.comment: Third in a bumper; not progressed over hurdles but quite interesting on h'cap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Third in a Ffos Las bumper on debut in November 2024 (2m, soft); not progressed as a hurdler, but quite interesting on his handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Genbu
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with good recent form, 2l-third at Uttoxeter 14 days ago off bottom weight
runners_data.comment: Juvenile winner for Sam England; good third to Spartan Times over C&D latest; interesting
runners_data.spotlight: Wetherby juvenile winner for Sam England last October (2m, good; first-time tongue-tie); some fair form since, and an interesting contender after his 2l-third to Spartan Times (who is now 4lb worse off) in a C&D handicap two weeks ago.

runners_data.name: Modern Style
runners_data.note: Hat-trick seeking hold-up horse, up 14lb but proven winner with strong recent form at Exeter/Taunton
runners_data.comment: On a hat-trick after wins on good at Exeter (2m) and Taunton (2m3f); up 14lb; contender
runners_data.spotlight: On a hat-trick having won novice handicaps at Exeter (2m, good) and Taunton (2m3f, good) last month; up 14lb (7lb for last win) but should be competitive again.

runners_data.name: Ask A Sainte

runners_data.comment: Best run for David Brace when 5th in maiden hurdle; interesting on h'cap/stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Best run for David Brace when fourth in a Wincanton maiden hurdle in December (1m7f, soft); that form is sound; an interesting contender on his handicap/stable debut.

runners_data.name: Merry Shuil
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare from same stable as Spartan Times, 81 days since last run over longer trip
runners_data.comment: Second in a Catterick mares' h'cap in February but not so good over 2m3f there latest
runners_data.spotlight: Best run over hurdles when runner-up in a mares' handicap at Catterick in February (1m7f, soft); lesser effort over 2m3f on same track last time (good to soft); others stronger.

races.paceDynamic: Spartan Times is the sole confirmed front runner and will control proceedings from the gate, likely setting a steady, sustainable tempo over this 2m trip without early pressure. The prominent runners Roarin' Success and Collanisi may track within striking distance, but the field is dominated by hold-up horses including Modern Style, Zafaan, Castle Quarter, Genbu, Ask A Sainte and Merry Shuil who will look to mount late challenges. With minimal early pace pressure and a single leader setting honest fractions, this race shape strongly favours the hold-up horses who can sit off the pace and unleash late kicks in the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Brigade Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Spartan Times sets honest pace without burning out early
scenarios.body: The steady tempo allows the patient hold-up horses to conserve energy and produce their best finishing efforts. Modern Style, Zafaan, or Castle Quarter benefit most from this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Spartan Times gets soft fractions and kicks clear turning in
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows the leader to dictate terms completely and build an unassailable advantage. Spartan Times proves too strong for the late challengers who leave themselves too much to do.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Roarin' Success or Collanisi position perfectly in behind the leader
scenarios.body: The tracking horses get first run on the leader while the hold-up brigade are still making ground from the back. This tactical positioning proves decisive in a steadily-run race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Spartan Times goes too slow and creates a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The crawling pace turns the race into a pure speed test over the final 3 furlongs. The most gifted athlete rather than the best-positioned horse wins in a blanket finish.

watchPoints.text: Spartan Times must be monitored early - if he gets uncontested soft fractions, the hold-up horses may have too much ground to make up
Modern Style carries a 14lb penalty for his recent wins and needs watching if the pace becomes truly testing
Castle Quarter returns from a 53-day break and requires monitoring for signs of rustiness in the early stages
Ask A Sainte makes his debut for new trainer Olly Murphy and watch for any market moves indicating stable confidence
The overall pace development needs watching - if Spartan Times goes too steady, expect a cavalry charge from the rear
